name: GEIS Encoder
description: Geometric Information Encoding System — the bidirectional, lossless converter between geometric tokens and binary. Operates in dense mode [vertex_bits][operator][symbol] preserving full geometric structure, or collapse mode for flat binary compatibility. State tensors (3×3 matrices) handle eigenvalues and projections for geometric transformations.

core_attributes.pattern: bidirectional geometric-binary translation, state tensor projection, lossless encoding

scope.definition: Round-trip encoding fidelity of geometric information encoding — fraction of original geometric data structure recoverable after encode-decode cycle using projective geometry mappings.

evidence.source: Coolidge (1940) 'A History of Geometrical Methods', Oxford UP; algebraic geometry encoding in Griffiths & Harris (1978) 'Principles of Algebraic Geometry', Wiley.
cross_domain_examples: projective transformation: lossless invertible for non-degenerate cases — 100% fidelity for well-conditioned inputs
Fourier encoding: information-theoretic reversibility when Nyquist condition met
DNA information storage: 0.98 round-trip fidelity demonstrated in Church et al. (2012) encoding experiment

scope.falsifiability: If geometric encoding-decoding cycles show cumulative error growth exceeding 1% per cycle for stable geometries, the lossless encoding claim requires qualification.
scope.measurement_limits: Fidelity is numerically conditioned — ill-conditioned geometric cases (near-degenerate configurations) produce error amplification. Floating-point precision limits fidelity to ~10⁻¹⁵ for 64-bit arithmetic.
